column2: Machine translation has improved dramatically over the past decade, driven largely by advances in neural network architectures and the availability of large parallel corpora. Early statistical systems relied on phrase tables and hand-tuned features, which made them brittle when faced with unfamiliar domains or long-distance reordering. Modern transformer-based models, by contrast, learn contextual representations that capture syntax and meaning across entire sentences, and in many language pairs they now produce output that professional translators consider fluent.
